message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | TxDOT – “Hands‑Free” Law | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑Tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI Enforcement | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield” signs give priority to the vehicle already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing on either side of a stopped bus with flashing red lights. | TxDOT – School Bus Safety | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other drivers.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the driver is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or stop sign.
• No parking in handicap spaces unless you have a valid permit. | TxDOT – Parking Rules | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Cameras enforce speed limits, red‑light violations, and other infractions. | TxDOT – Automated Enforcement | | **Emergency Vehicle Exemptions** | • Drivers may exceed speed limits and ignore traffic signals when following an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | • Texas has several toll roads (e.g., Sam Houston Tollway).
• Electronic toll collection (TxTag) is required for some. | TxDOT – Toll Roads | ### How to Stay Updated - **TxDOT Website** – Official rules, updates, and driver resources. - **TxDMV** – Registration, licensing, and inspection requirements. - **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text (available online). - **Local County Courts** – For specific local ordinances or recent changes. --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. 2. **Avoid distractions** – especially cell‑phone use; hands‑free is the safest option. 3. **Observe speed limits** – they’re enforced rigorously, especially on rural interstates. 4. **Respect school buses** – stop and wait until the bus resumes motion. 5. **Check your vehicle’s inspection status** – an expired inspection can lead to fines or impoundment. If you need more detailed information on a specific law or want to check the latest updates, let me know!
